clues.title: Google car: Unique car
text: If you see a snorkel on the Google car, you’re in Kenya.
However, the car is sometimes seen without it, so don’t rule out Kenya if the snorkel isn’t visible.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Coverage: Bird poop
text: Only on a very tiny bit of coverage on the C104 in southern Kenya, embedded in Tsavo National Park, the Google car is adorned with two recognizable splats of bird poop. Cheers.

text: The area around Kitui is semi-arid, usually mountainous, and has light orange, sandy dirt.

clues.title: Landscape: Mombasa White Sand
text: Mombasa and the other coastal towns are easily identified from the white sandy soil, palm trees and coastal feel.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Agriculture Parts
text: The far west areas of the country that are northwest and southwest of Kisumu are the most agricultural parts of the country.
You will often see farms, grassy hills, and tall eucalyptus trees in this region of the country.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Coverage: A1 Northwest
text: The northwest part of the country has very limited coverage, most of which is on the A1 or in Sibiloi National Park.
It has faintly tan soil and sparse low trees.
A lot of the coverage in this area is very flat, but you can also see hills or mountains.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: A109 Cord & Orange Dirt
text: The A109 between Mombasa and Nairobi has light orange dirt and many hills around the road and in the distance.
Most of the coverage between Mombasa and Emali also has a unique car, which has a cord on the left.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Dirt Car
text: This car that is covered in specks of dirt is unique to these stretches of the A3, B9, and the Habaswein-Dadaab Road connecting the two.

clues.title: Google car: Gen 4 Cars
text: Kenya has many unique Google cars, almost all of which will have visible car meta.
In Generation 3 you will typically see a car with a roof rack and a snorkel.
In Generation 4 you will always have a large pickup truck, which will either be white or grey.
The grey car comes in two slightly different variations, of which one can either be with or without a snorkel.
It is the only country other than Mongolia with a snorkel.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Kerio Lodwar Region
text: The area surrounding and between Kerio and Lodwar uses the same car as the Aberdare National Park, but with a vastly different landscape. It is very sandy, dry, and has little vegetation.

clues.title: Google car: Amboseli National Park
text: Amboseli National Park has a grey car with a small snorkel. It is very flat with tan grass, few trees, and dried up lake beds. You can always see the base of Kilimanjaro to the south, with most of it obscured by clouds.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Mara Triangle

clues.title: Vegetation: B9
text: The B9 in the Northeast is entirely unpaved and has bright reddish orange dirt with many trees surrounding the road. Most of it is very flat, but the coverage at the western end of the road can have hills and mountains. The soil also transitions into a more sandy colour.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: A2 between Isiolo and Marsabit
text: The A2 between Isiolo and Marsabit has many plants alongside the road and you will often see large mountains in the distance. The stretch going through Namunyak Wildlife Conservation Trust will have a very large mountain range to the west.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: A2 north of Marsabit
text: A2 north of Marsabit will be much flatter, with some mountains in the distance. The stretch just north or Marsabit will have mountains visible to the south, while further north, a different range can be seen. It will also have much less vegetation.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: A3 north of Garissa
text: The A3 north of Garissa is very unique, with light coloured soil and many green trees on either side of the road.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Western part of the C34
text: The western part of the C34 is a flat, east to west road. There are two long, straight sections with an abundance of sugar cane. Furthermore, you will see a large mountain range north along the entire mentioned stretches of road.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Nairobi
text: Nairobi is the largest city in the country, and capital of Kenya. It is the only city to have a considerable amount of skyscrapers, and is highly developed. It is densely populated, and is surrounded by small, poor settlements.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Coverage: Mt Kilimanjaro
text: In a lot of the coverage north of Mt Kilimanjaro, the mountain is visible to the south, usually obscured by clouds. In the city of Oloitoktok, the mountain will often be visible directly to the south.
NOTE: The map shows the location of Mt Kilimanjaro, but it can be seen from very far away.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Google car: Amboseli National Park
text: Amboseli National Park has a grey car with a small snorkel. It is very flat with tan grass, few trees, and dried up lake beds. You can always see the base of Kilimanjaro to the south, with most of it obscured by clouds.

clues.title: Google car: Aberdare National Park
text: Aberdare National Park has a grey and brown car that features a large snorkel. Almost all of the coverage is outside of the National Park, with only two roads within the park covered. The main road through the park has these rubber bands on the roof rack, which can only be found in one other National Park in Kenya.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Rubber bands
text: Between Kitale and Mt Elgon, you can find the Aberdare car as well, but it will always have rubber bands, unlike in Aberdare where it will only have them on the main roads through the park. It can be differentiated from Aberdare by its redder dirt, and greener landscape.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Google car: Kerio-Lodwar area
text: The area surrounding and between Kerio and Lodwar uses a grey and brown car that features a large snorkel. It is very sandy, dry, and has little vegetation.
